Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Goal: Migrate Nova Search's current embedding pipeline off VendorX while keeping embedding dimensions and search latency stable for your semantic recall features.
- Key constraints: existing vectors are 1536 dims, ~25M vectors, batch ingestion peaks at ~2000 reqs/min during reindex windows, and normalization applied as L2 on VendorX outputs.
- Integration needs: SDK auth (API key rotation), streaming ingestion, batch normalization, and an optional reranker pipeline for prioritizing results on long-tail queries.

Open technical items (next steps):
1) Confirm whether you want to keep 1536 dims or accept a smaller dimension with quantization tradeoffs.
2) Share a sample of your schema + a few example records for mapping (we requested 100 rows).
3) Decide on a migration strategy: bulk reindex now vs. hybrid (reindex on read).
4) Confirm SSO/KMS requirements for Private deployment if you choose on-prem.

I've looped in Vivek (solutions) for the migration plan and Neha (applied ML/inference) for the embedding dimension and batching recommendations.

Attachments: I attached a short migration plan and a CSV template for schema mapping.

Proposed next calls: Technical deep-dive with Neha (30-45m) — available Wed/Thu this week.

Hi all —

Thanks for the context and the sample. Quick recommendations based on the sample and scale: 

1) Dimensions: Keep 1536 for parity with VendorX for the initial migration. This minimizes semantic drift; once migrated we can run a model-compression A/B to evaluate 1024 dims with quantization (INT8) for a small perf/cost win.

2) Normalization: Continue L2-normalization before storage. VendorX applies L2 on their embeddings; mismatched normalization is the common root cause of quality regressions. Add a lightweight schema flag to indicate "normalized": true so downstream rerankers don't re-normalize.

3) Batching/ingestion: For bulk reindex use batched writes in chunks of 5k-10k vectors (our ingestion API supports streaming + bulk JSONL). For real-time ingestion, target micro-batches of 64-256 depending on vector size; with 1536 dims we typically see best throughput/latency tradeoff around 128 items per batch on p3/p4-class nodes. Throttle to keep tail latency under SLOs (we can suggest client-side backoff/queueing).

4) Migration strategy: Hybrid approach is safest — reindex cold docs during off-peak windows and reindex on read for hot docs. We'll provide reindex tooling and a checkpointed job to avoid duplicates.

5) VendorX quirks: Watch for tokenization differences if embeddings were produced by different LM families. We should run a small cross-embedding similarity audit (50-200 pairs) post-migration. Also confirm if VendorX applied PCA or post-processing; we should be able to detect it via variance analysis.

6) Auth/SDK notes: Use API keys with rotation; for Private deployments we support Vault + KMS integration (Neha will be on the call to confirm audit/logging requirements). SDKs support streaming ingestion and retries with idempotency keys.

Suggested agenda for Wed 08/19 10:00 PT (30m):
- 5m: Quick status + constraints (Samir)
- 10m: Neha: dimensions/normalization/batching and migration proposal
- 10m: Vivek: implementation plan, timing, and SLA / KMS options
- 5m: Agree next steps and ownership

I'll bring a short checklist and a migration-runbook stub.

-Neha
